did_you_know.text: Gerar is generally associated with the western Negev, but its exact location is uncertain.
In the Bible, dreams sometimes serve as a way to convey a divine message; here, Abimelech receives a warning in a dream.
This is the first place in the Torah where Abraham is explicitly called a “prophet.” Here, his role is also connected with praying for someone else.
Sarah was Abraham’s half-sister: they shared a father but not a mother. In modern terms, this was a close family relationship.
The phrase “a covering for the eyes” appears only here in the Bible, so its exact meaning is uncertain. Commentators have offered different explanations.
The repetition “completely stopped” is a biblical style used to emphasize something total or prolonged. Here, it stresses that all the wombs in Abimelech’s household had been closed.
